title: Simplify in ChatGPT, Claude and Codex (MCP)
summary: AI job search in ChatGPT or Claude: find jobs, tailor your resume for each role and auto apply to jobs without leaving the chat. See a real session and prompts.
body_markdown:
Simplify now works inside ChatGPT, Claude and Codex, so you can run your AI job search from the chat you already have open. Ask in plain words for jobs that fit you, a tailored copy of your resume from the[AI Resume Builder](https://simplify.jobs/resume-builder?utm_source=blog&utm_medium=cta&utm_campaign=use-simplify-in-chatgpt-claude-codex&utm_content=body-1) , a rundown of your[Job Tracker](https://simplify.jobs/job-application-tracker?utm_source=blog&utm_medium=cta&utm_campaign=use-simplify-in-chatgpt-claude-codex&utm_content=body-2) , or to auto apply to a job with[Autopilot](https://simplify.jobs/ai-auto-apply?utm_source=blog&utm_medium=cta&utm_campaign=use-simplify-in-chatgpt-claude-codex&utm_content=body-3) . It's included with[Simplify+](https://simplify.jobs/plus?utm_source=blog&utm_medium=cta&utm_campaign=use-simplify-in-chatgpt-claude-codex&utm_content=body-4) ; free Simplify accounts can't connect it. Here's how to connect it, then a real session from start to finish and the prompts worth trying first.


## Add the Simplify ChatGPT plugin or Claude connector


The quickest way to connect is to paste this into ChatGPT, Claude, Claude Code or Codex, and the assistant sets it up for you:


```text
Please set up https://simplify.jobs/mcp/setup.md
```


When you sign in, check **Apply and update your profile** if you want it to save jobs, tailor resumes or apply for you. Step-by-step setup for each app, with videos, plus permissions, troubleshooting and how to disconnect, is in[our help center guide](https://help.simplify.jobs/en/articles/8107058-use-simplify-in-claude-chatgpt-and-codex-mcp?utm_source=blog&utm_medium=cta&utm_campaign=use-simplify-in-chatgpt-claude-codex&utm_content=body-5) .


## Why we built this


You probably already have ChatGPT or Claude open while you job search. You paste in a job description. Then your resume. You ask it to compare the two. Then you switch tabs and do the actual applying somewhere else.


So we connected the two: once you add Simplify, the assistant reads your real Simplify account: your matches, your resumes, your preferences and your Job Tracker. You don't have to paste your resume in or explain your search from the beginning. And if you let it, it can also save jobs, tailor a resume copy and send applications through Autopilot, all from the same chat.


That last part is the difference from most job apps in ChatGPT. Indeed's ChatGPT app, for example, sends you to Indeed to start your application. With Simplify, the chat can apply for you.


(The technical name for this is an MCP server. In ChatGPT it shows up as a plugin, and in Claude as a connector. You don't need to know what any of that means to use it.)


Once it's connected, you can try the same messages yourself. Here's what that looks like.


## What a real session looks like


Here's a full session in ChatGPT on the web, on a test account we set up as a backend engineer with two years of experience. Each step below is a message you can copy (swap in the company you want); the screenshots show what came back for our test account.


**1. "Find jobs that match my Simplify profile and explain why each one fits me."**


It pulled the account's saved preferences (junior to mid-level, full-time, Seattle, the Bay Area, New York or remote, $120K and up) and came back with six roles as job cards. For each one it said why it fits, using the actual resume: for a Notion infrastructure role, it pointed to a bullet about cutting API latency from 820 ms to 310 ms. It also listed a catch for each one, like "requires three office days per week".


**2. "Tailor a copy of my resume for the \[company\] role and show me what you changed."**


We picked the Notion role (and, in the same message, asked it to save the Twitch job, which it did). It made a new resume for Notion, leaving the original alone. Then it showed a table of every change and why it helps for that role, plus one bullet before and after. Every number stayed the same, and it said no experience was added.


**3. "Apply to the \[company\] job with Autopilot."**


That's a direct instruction, so it applied. It used the Notion resume it had just made, turned off extra tailoring so that version went in as is, and sent back a link to follow the run. The application showed as submitted a few minutes later.


**4. "Summarize my Job Tracker, tell me what to follow up on, and how many Autopilot credits I have left."**


It counted the tracker (18 jobs, 8 applied, 5 rejected), showed 99 of 100 credits left with the refresh date, and ranked what to follow up on and when. It also suggested archiving the rejections, and said it hadn't changed anything. (If you're still choosing where to track applications, here's[how the Simplify Job Tracker compares with Teal, Huntr and Notion](https://simplify.jobs/blog/best-job-application-trackers-2026?ref=blog.simplify.jobs) .)


That's one session on a test account, so don't read it as a promise of how every chat goes.


## AI job search prompts to try first


Start a new chat and mention Simplify in your first message (in ChatGPT, type @Simplify), so the assistant knows to use it. Then keep going in the same chat. These worked in our testing:


- *Why is the second one a good fit for me?*
- *Show me more.*
- *Save the first one.*
- *Tailor my resume for that job.*
- *Can I apply to it with Autopilot?*
- *What did I apply to this week?*


My favorite is a visa one: *Use Simplify to find jobs that match my preferences and sponsor visas, and tell me what you couldn't verify.* The last half is the point. Sponsorship info comes from company-level data and is missing for a lot of companies, so "unknown" doesn't mean a company won't sponsor. Asking the assistant to say what it couldn't verify makes that visible, and then you check the job post or ask the employer.


For prompts that don't need a Simplify connection, see[how to use ChatGPT or Claude to write your resume](https://simplify.jobs/blog/how-to-use-chatgpt-to-write-and-improve-your-resume?ref=blog.simplify.jobs) ,[5 ChatGPT prompts to find a new job](https://simplify.jobs/blog/5-chatgpt-prompts-to-find-a-new-job?ref=blog.simplify.jobs) , and, once interviews start,[how to prep for job interviews with ChatGPT](https://simplify.jobs/blog/chatgpt-job-interview-prep?ref=blog.simplify.jobs) .


## Auto apply to jobs from a chat


[Autopilot](https://simplify.jobs/ai-auto-apply?utm_source=blog&utm_medium=cta&utm_campaign=use-simplify-in-chatgpt-claude-codex&utm_content=body-6) is Simplify's AI auto apply feature: it submits supported applications for you, without a final review step. In a chat, it applies when you tell it to, like in step 3 above. If you'd rather check first, ask instead ("Can I apply to it with Autopilot?"): it lists the job, the resume and your tailoring settings and waits for your yes. It uses the same weekly Autopilot credits that come with Simplify+.


If you want the backstory on Autopilot, I wrote about[why we built Autopilot and what happened when I used it with my own resume](https://simplify.jobs/blog/why-we-built-autopilot?ref=blog.simplify.jobs) .


## Common questions


**What is a job search MCP?** MCP (Model Context Protocol) is the open standard that lets AI assistants like ChatGPT, Claude and Codex connect to other apps. A job search MCP connects your assistant to a job platform, so it can look up jobs and, depending on the platform, act on your behalf. Simplify's covers the whole loop: your matches, your resumes, your Job Tracker and applying with Autopilot.


**Is there a LinkedIn or Indeed MCP for job search?** Indeed has an official connector in Claude's directory. It searches Indeed listings, shows job details and gives you links, and you apply on Indeed's site. We couldn't find an official LinkedIn MCP; the LinkedIn MCP servers out there are community projects, and some work by using your logged-in session or scraping, so check LinkedIn's terms before you try one. Simplify's MCP works from your own Simplify account, so it can also tailor your resume and apply for you.


**Can an AI agent apply to jobs for me?** With Simplify, yes. Ask ChatGPT or Claude to apply to a job and Autopilot submits supported applications for you, using your resume and saved answers. It only applies when you tell it to, there's no final review step, and each successful application uses one Autopilot credit.


**How do I use ChatGPT or Claude for my job search?** Without a connection, you paste in job descriptions and your resume and ask for help;[these ChatGPT prompts to find a new job](https://simplify.jobs/blog/5-chatgpt-prompts-to-find-a-new-job?ref=blog.simplify.jobs) are a good start. With the Simplify MCP connected, you skip the pasting: the assistant already sees your matches, resumes and Job Tracker, so you can ask "find jobs that fit me" or "tailor my resume for this one" directly.


**Is the Simplify MCP free?** No. It's part of[Simplify+](https://simplify.jobs/plus?utm_source=blog&utm_medium=cta&utm_campaign=use-simplify-in-chatgpt-claude-codex&utm_content=body-7) , the same plan that includes Autopilot. Free Simplify accounts can sign in but can't connect it to ChatGPT or Claude.


## Try it


If you're on Simplify+, open the assistant you already use and paste *Please set up https://simplify.jobs/mcp/setup.md* . If you're not,[here's what Simplify+ includes](https://simplify.jobs/plus?utm_source=blog&utm_medium=cta&utm_campaign=use-simplify-in-chatgpt-claude-codex&utm_content=body-8) .
